title: How small can a star get?

narration.heading: Tiny stars
narration.text: You think stars are giant balls of fire? Some dead ones are tiny.

narration.heading: Neutron star
narration.text: This is a neutron star, the crushed core left by a supernova. It's only about twenty kilometres wide.

narration.heading: Spinning
narration.text: The fastest one known spins over seven hundred times a second.

narration.heading: The Moon
narration.text: Our Moon is far bigger, about three and a half thousand kilometres across.

narration.heading: Sirius B
narration.text: Sirius B is a white dwarf, another dead star, a little smaller than Earth.

narration.heading: Heavy stuff
narration.text: It holds about as much mass as the Sun. One cubic centimetre of it weighs about a tonne.

narration.heading: Earth
narration.text: Earth is only slightly bigger than Sirius B.

narration.heading: The Sun
narration.text: And the Sun is about a hundred times wider. One point three million Earths could fit inside.

narration.heading: The twist
narration.text: The twist? That tiny neutron star outweighs the Sun. A teaspoon of it would weigh over five billion tonnes.

narration.heading: One day
narration.text: One day, our Sun will become a white dwarf too. Which dead star would you visit?

skit.text: Five billion tonnes in a teaspoon? I'll stick to my sugar, thanks.

titles: What if you lined up the smallest stars?
A star the size of a city that outweighs the Sun
youtube.description: A neutron star, our Moon, the white dwarf Sirius B, Earth and the Sun side by side at true scale, and how the smallest of them outweighs the Sun.

sources.claim: Neutron stars have a radius on the order of 10 km and a mass of about 1.4 solar masses; they form from a supernova; the fastest known spins 716.35 times per second; a teaspoon of the material would have a mass over 5.5×10¹² kg
A white dwarf packs a Sun-like mass into an Earth-sized volume, with a density of about 1 tonne per cubic centimetre
Sirius B is a white dwarf with a radius of 5,634 km and a mass of 1.018 solar masses
The Moon's mean radius is 1,737.4 km
The Sun's radius is about 700,000 km, about 100 times Earth's width; 1.3 million Earths would fill it; it will become a white dwarf in about 5 billion years
